title: Geometry nodes, edited live
blurb: Buildify, a flower field and a DSL terrain as geometry-nodes modifiers, edited live in the editor.
line: Buildify 21 ms · flowers 496 ms · terrain 396 ms per input change (mean of 4, GPU VM)
intro: Blender 5.2.2 geometry-nodes groups evaluated in TypeScript on the mesh kernel, as modifiers in the threepipe modelling editor. Buildify 1.0's building generator and Blender Studio's flower field come from their .blend files through the blendAsset command (node groups, inputs and the objects they read - nothing Blender evaluated); the terrain is a group written in the TypeScript DSL. Each is edited twice: in Properties > Modifiers with the mouse and keyboard, and through the modifier update command an agent sends - every edit one undo step, re-running only what it reaches.

how:
record.mjs opens examples/procedural-editor-assets once per asset on the GPU VM, clicks the Modifiers tab, types the new value into the field and presses Enter (real Playwright input), waits for the object's evaluated mesh to change and records that time, then sends four timed modifier update commands. demos/shared/film.mjs renders and captures every frame, so an evaluation that takes seconds shows as its number on screen rather than a frozen picture. Times are wall time in the page on the VM (6 cores, Apple Paravirtual GPU).

Re-run: put the bundles in tmp/bundles/ (plugins/procedural/tests/fixtures/ASSETS.md), node demos/geometry-nodes/record.mjs, pull tmp/demo/geometry-nodes/film/ to demos/geometry-nodes/film/, node demos/geometry-nodes/make-report.mjs. The track-2 acceptance record (scripts/procedural-acceptance-video.mjs) is the same run in real time.
weak: Buildify and the flower field are third-party assets: their renders and this film cannot be committed or published until their use in launch material is decided.
The editor viewport lighting is the editor default; the flower field's grass reads as flat colour at 1080p.
The editor frames each asset with its own frame-all, so the terrain sits small in the viewport, and the selection box (red) stays on throughout, because the modifier panel needs the object selected.
